provenance.title: DERIVED HIGHER HOCHSCHILD HOMOLOGY, TOPOLOGICAL CHIRAL HOMOLOGY AND FACTORIZATION ALGEBRAS
provenance.authors: GRÉGORY GINOT, THOMAS TRADLER, AND MAHMOUD ZEINALIAN

candidates.statement: In our context, the $(\infty,1)$-categories we considered are obtained by a Dwyer-Kan localization process from standard model categories, though the results of this paper should not depend on the particular chosen approach to $(\infty,1)$-categories, see also Remark [\[R:non-unique\]](#R:non-unique){reference-type="ref" reference="R:non-unique"}.

It should satisfy a ''cosheaf-like'' condition, meaning that $\mathcal{F}(V)$ can be computed by Čech complexes indexed on nice enough covers, called factorizing covers, see [@CG] and Section [\[S:Factorization\]](#S:Factorization){reference-type="ref" reference="S:Factorization"}.
Since a CDGA $C$ is an $E_k$-algebra (as well as an $\mathbb{E}_{M}^{\otimes}$-algebra) for all $k$, $\int_M C$ should not be able to distinguish different framings.
Since manifolds embed in euclidean spaces, we further see that $\int_M C$ should makes sense for *any* manifold.
This hints that any deformation retract of a manifold should also have a well defined topological chiral homology (with value in a $C$) equivalent to the one of the manifold.
However, it is also possible to work with simplicial commutative algebras, and all our results should makes sense in this setting.

Note that a simplicial set is determined by its $(\infty, 0)$ path groupoid and therefore the category of simplicial sets should be thought of as the $(\infty, 1)$ category of all $(\infty, 0)$ groupoids.

Building upon the last remark, we see that the topological chiral homology of an $(m+k)$-framed manifold $M$ with value in a CDGA should be equivalent (up to neglect of structure) to the topological chiral homology of $M$ equipped with the stable normal framing so that we get

candidates.statement: The Blob complex $\mathcal{B}_*(M,\mathcal{C}^{C_{\scriptstyle\bullet}(\Omega^{n} Y)})$ for non-necessarily closed manifolds shall not be mistaken with the Blob complex associated to the $A_\infty$-$n$-category associated to the fundamental groupoid of the space $Y$ in [@MW § 6] (though the construction share some similarities).

Theorem [\[T:HF=TCH\]](#T:HF=TCH){reference-type="ref" reference="T:HF=TCH"} below and Proposition [\[P:blob\]](#P:blob){reference-type="ref" reference="P:blob"} suggest that the blob complex should be closely related to Factorization algebras as well.
